extracted.intended_audience: Tufts faculty, instructional developers, and university stakeholders interested in CELT grant-funded projects
extracted.subtask_description: Summaries of CELT-associated grant projects and their stated aims (what the grants fund/support and the pedagogical priorities they promote). Useful for understanding institutional grant focus and themes for educational-development funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Davis Educational Foundation — Faculty Awakenings in a Time of Crisis (project goals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote the continuation of positive and productive pedagogical practices adopted during the period during COVID that necessitated remote teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of practices to be continued include a more learner-centered stance, reflective practice, attention to marginalized student perspectives and experiences, and the use of technology for engagement. Project is a collaboration between CELT and the Institute for Research on Learning and Education (IRLI) with named leads (Annie Soisson, David Hammer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI) Grant — diversity and instructional support
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant designed to boost diversity in the natural sciences by funding a five-year initiative that provides Tufts science faculty and teaching assistants in introductory science courses with support to enhance their ability to elicit, recognize, interpret, and respond meaningfully to all students’ thinking and reasoning regardless of their cultural background or prior preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded by HHMI in 2017 ($1 million). Emphasizes support for faculty and TAs in introductory courses, inclusive pedagogical practice, and improving recognition/response to diverse student thinking; lists project leaders (Roger Tobin, David Hammer, Mitch McVey, Diren Turner, Annie Soisson).

rubrics_metrics.name: POD Network Research Grant — interrogating values in educational development
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims to promote a greater culture of evidence-based research designed to contribute new knowledge in the fields of educational, instructional, and organizational development; specifically to examine educational development’s values in order to interrogate the field for racism and colonization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes a multi-institutional collaboration using a number of sources and methods to (1) gain a comprehensive picture of the values held by educational developers today and (2) uncover who has and has not been included in the shaping of those values. Named investigators include Heather Dwyer (Tufts), Marisella Rodriguez (UC Berkeley), and Jamiella Brooks (University of Pennsylvania).

rubrics_metrics.name: CELT grant thematic priorities (implicit cross-cutting criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Across listed projects, grants prioritize sustaining learner-centered and reflective pedagogies adopted during COVID, promoting inclusive teaching that attends to marginalized student perspectives, fostering evidence-based research in educational development, supporting multi-institutional collaboration, and interrogating racism and colonization within the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This synthesis is drawn from the projects described: continuation of remote-era positive practices (learner-centered stance, reflective practice, technology for engagement), boosting diversity in STEM teaching and TA support, and systematic research to surface values and inclusion/exclusion in educational development.
